title: epochal-quant-regression-during-scaleout-action-plan
creator: Aisha Moreno
description: Summary: During two customer-facing capacity scaleout events (autoscaling add-node), a subset of quantized transformer models experienced periodic accuracy regressions and intermittent worker crashloops. Symptoms appeared as elevated BLEU/ROUGE degradation and model-serving OOMs/crashloops for models using a legacy per-deployment quant metadata format. Impact: affected 12% of serving capacity for a 90-minute window; several customers reported increased error rates and degraded quality. This ticket tracks investigation, mitigations, and long-term fixes.
reproduction_steps: 1) Provision a 4-node Dedicated pool with mix of quantized model variants (legacy .qmeta and new format)
2) Trigger concurrent scaleout by simulating 500 qps ramp with short-lived sessions to force model reloads and eviction
3) Observe routing to new nodes and the model loader selecting quant mode based on on-disk .qmeta; note mismatch between loader kernel table and runtime kernel index
4) Measure generation quality with a standardized eval prompt set (eval-suite/quant-epochal-regression) before and after scaleout
root_cause_summary: When nodes join during autoscale, a race in the model loader copies a per-deployment 'quant epoch' marker from an older artifact into the node cache. This marker is used by kernel-selector to pick optimized fused ops. For artifacts produced before the runtime kernel-index remap (older epoch), the selector occasionally chose kernels incompatible with current fused attention codepaths, producing subtle numerical drift and triggering a GC-induced OOM on warm-up sequences. The combination of kernel mismatch and cache-eviction timings caused periodic accuracy regressions and crashloops during bursty scaleouts.
mitigations: Hotfix: block auto-attach of legacy .qmeta artifacts during autoscale. New nodes will only accept artifacts with explicit runtime-epoch >= runtime-1.22 until validation patch is deployed
Fallback: enable conservative kernel-selector mode for pools serving quantized models (disables some fused kernels, increases latency slightly but prevents drift)
Rollback: provide a temporary cluster flag to pin serving pools to pre-scaleout model versions for affected customers
action_items: (A1) Deploy validation layer in model loader to reject or remap legacy quant metadata on startup (owner: Liam, estimate: 3) - target: 2026-03-18
(A2) Add cross-node canary for quant-epoch compatibility on every autoscale event; fail-open to conservative kernel-selector if mismatch detected (owner: Priya Rao, estimate: 5) - target: 2026-03-22
(A3) Create an automated nightly batch test that simulates scaleout with mixed-epoch artifacts and runs eval-suite/quant-epochal-regression (owner: QA team, estimate: 3) - target: 2026-03-26
(A4) Update model onboarding docs and artifact signing to include explicit runtime-epoch metadata and validator schema (owner: Platform Docs, estimate: 2) - target: 2026-03-30
(A5) Post-incident customer communication and RCA note with mitigation steps and timeline (owner: SRE/CS, estimate: 1) - target: 2026-03-15
